Far across the curve of the world below, a green-and-violet aurora ripples in slow curtains over the night hemisphere, mirrored faintly in the dark ocean beneath.
A second tiny suited figure works far down the hull, their helmet-light a lone spark against the vast plating, tether a thin silver thread between them.
A meteor streaks past in the deep distance trailing a thin line of glowing ablation, burning silently against the star-field before winking out completely.
A distant spacecraft fires its thrusters on a slow approach, twin plasma-blue cones glowing softly, running-lights blinking as it closes from far across the void.
A solar flare erupts in a great luminous arc off the far limb of the sun, a slow-motion cathedral of plasma curling silently against the black.
A satellite catches the sun at a perfect angle and blazes into a brilliant white flare, holding for a breath before fading back into its quiet orbit.
Far below, a shooting star burns up in the upper atmosphere, a brief orange scratch of fire sliding along the curve of the planet and vanishing.
A slow shower of glittering debris tumbles through the deep background, each fragment catching sunlight in a lazy spinning constellation drifting silently across the frame.
A distant ship's running-lights blink a slow patient rhythm against the dark, red and green and white, impossibly tiny, crossing the void on some unhurried course.
A far-off explosion blooms silently in the deep distance, a brief orange-white flower of light expanding and fading without sound, leaving only a faint dispersing halo.
A vast debris field drifts in the deep background, broken hull plating and frozen gas catching sunlight in slow rotation, tumbling like a ruined archipelago through the void.
A comet traces its long pale tail across the far edge of frame, nucleus a faint smudge, the dust-veil stretching in a soft arc across the star-field.
Deep in the distance, two spacecraft rendezvous, one holding station while the other edges close, their combined running-lights forming a brief slow-moving constellation against the dark.
A brilliant pulse of laser light lances across the deep background, perhaps a ranging signal or data beam, thin and blue-white, gone in a fraction of a second.
Far across the hull in the deep background, a repair drone hovers on tiny thrusters, its work-lamp a warm yellow pinprick against the cold dark plating.
A distant planet catches full sunlight, its crescent sharp and pale at the very edge of the background, rings barely visible as a thin luminous line around it.
A gamma-ray burst afterglow smears a brief cold blue-white streak across the deep star-field in the far background, fading to nothing before it can be named.
Far below on the night side, a massive thunderstorm pulses with silent lightning, each flash illuminating a vast cloud system stretching across an entire continent in the dark.
A cluster of small cubesats drifts past in the deep background, their flat solar panels winking in sequence like slow blinking eyes as they tumble through orbital dawn.
A spent rocket stage cartwheels silently in the far distance, its white paint catching sunlight in a slow lazy roll, trailing a faint glitter of ice crystals.
A solar wind shock wave sweeps the deep background in a faint shimmering curtain, compressing the magnetosphere and sparking pale aurora along the planet's distant terminator line.
Far across the void a resupply vessel fires its retro-rockets to decelerate, the brief orange-white bloom of engine fire soft and silent at this impossible distance.
A thin band of the Milky Way fills the deep background, dense with cold light, a river of a hundred billion suns pouring silently behind the station hull.
A pressure-relief vent on a distant module fires a brief plume of white vapor into vacuum, the cloud expanding instantly into a glittering ice-crystal halo and dissolving.
Far down the orbital track, a derelict station tumbles slowly, its broken solar arrays catching and losing the sun in a long melancholy rotation against the star-field.
